meta.description: Adaptive learning rate and feature weighting

user.t:
Rust crate C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh. Read DESIGN.md, src/router.rs, src/hebbian.rs, src/sim.rs, src/stats.rs, src/bin/experiment.rs, results/experiment_output.txt. Toolchain: in every Bash call first run
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:/c/Users/mariu/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Packages/BrechtSanders.WinLibs.POSIX.UCRT_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe/mingw64/bin:$PATH"

Goal: make the Hebbian router learn better, judged ONLY by held-out paired statistics. Current state: tuned Hebbian (eta 0.05, temp 0.02, decay 0.001) gets .734 on held-out seeds 31-60 vs keyword .6995; default settings do not beat keyword, so the rule is fragile to its learning rate.

YOUR FILES: src/hebbian.rs (you own it now; keep the HebbianRouter public API, HebbianConfig field names, Default values and serde compatibility — add new fields with #[serde(default)] and keep new behaviour OFF by default) and a NEW bench binary src/bin/router_lab.rs (do not edit experiment.rs, sim.rs, stats.rs, mesh.rs, variants.rs, main.rs — other agents own them; use sim.rs/stats.rs read-only through their public API; if the sim API changes under you, adapt).

Implement and evaluate, each as an opt-in option:
1. Self-tuning learning rate ("meta-learning"): per-feature-row adaptive eta driven by surprise — e.g. a Page-Hinkley or CUSUM drift detector on (reward - baseline) per row that boosts eta (and temporarily temperature/epsilon) when a change is detected and anneals it back when stable; or a sign-agreement (Delta-Bar-Delta / RPROP-style) per-row step size. Goal: one setting that works without hand-tuning eta and recovers faster after drift.
2. Feature reliability weighting: learn per-feature weights (e.g. running predictiveness/entropy of each feature's best agent, or an IDF-like down-weighting of features that appear across many task types) so confound keywords stop dominating the score.
3. Optional: optimistic initialisation / UCB-style exploration bonus for rarely tried (feature, agent) cells instead of flat epsilon.
router_lab.rs: same protocol as experiment.rs — tune ONLY on seeds 1-8, evaluate on held-out seeds 31-60, paired per-seed diffs with 95% t-CI. Compare: hebbian default, hebbian-tuned (current best), and each new option alone and combined, at DEFAULT settings (the point is robustness without tuning) and tuned. Report drift-recovery (early-post window) and regret. Write results/router_lab.json.
Acceptance: an option counts as an improvement only if its paired CI vs hebbian-tuned excludes 0 on held-out seeds (or it matches hebbian-tuned while needing no tuning, which you must show with CIs). Add unit tests for each option. cargo test --release green. Do not git commit. Final report: what helped, what didn't (with numbers), and the recommended default config.

handback.t:
None of the three options beats the best fair baseline. On held-out seeds 31-60 (fixed world, 2000 tasks, tuned on seeds 1-8 only), the best fair baseline is hebbian-tuned (0.7341). No option's paired CI vs it excludes 0 in the positive direction at any horizon. The Hebbian family does not beat the fair bandits. Hebbian-tuned and untuned eps-greedy(.99,.02) are statistically tied: -0.0035 [-0.0174,+0.0103] for eps-greedy vs tuned.

Tests and files:
- `cargo test --release --lib` passes (71 tests, including 8 new ones for the options).
- The full `cargo test --release` currently fails to compile `src/bin/experiment.rs` (missing `Spec::Thompson`, a `par_map` argument mismatch). That is another agent's mid-edit file. I did not touch it and did not run the bin tests.
- Nothing was committed.

**What I built** (`src/hebbian.rs`; public API, field names and defaults unchanged; new fields are `#[serde(default)]` and everything is off by default, with a test that the default path is unchanged and old configs still load):
1. `meta` (MetaKind):
   - **PageHinkley**: per-row eta starts at `eta` as a ceiling and anneals geometrically to `meta_eta_floor`. A two-sided CUSUM drift detector snaps it back to the ceiling and raises epsilon and temperature through a decaying alert.
   - **Dbd**: delta-bar-delta per-row step size.
2. `weighting` (WeightKind: Idf, Entropy, Contrast): per-feature reliability multipliers, normalised to mean 1 so the temperature keeps its meaning.
3. `ucb_c` and `ucb_discount`: an exploration bonus `c/sqrt(1+n_fa)` on rarely tried (feature, agent) cells, with discounted counts so stale cells regain the bonus.

`src/bin/router_lab.rs` follows the experiment.rs protocol and also runs the fair baselines, horizons 500/1000/2000/6000, an eta x temperature sweep, and extra worlds. It writes `results/router_lab.json`.

**Held-out results, 2000 tasks, success (paired diff vs hebbian-tuned):**
- keyword: 0.6995, -0.035 SIG
- eps-greedy(.99,.02), untuned: 0.7306, -0.0035 n.s.
- pooled-ts(.99): 0.7033, -0.031 SIG
- pooled-ts(1.0): 0.7197, not shown against the reference in the output I reviewed.
- hebbian-default: 0.6927, -0.041 SIG
- hebbian-tuned: 0.7341 (reference)
- [def] meta-ph: 0.7320, -0.0022 [-0.0132,+0.0089] n.s.
- [def] meta-dbd: 0.7037, -0.030 SIG
- [def] weight-idf / entropy / contrast: 0.6936 / 0.6885 / 0.6883, all about -0.04 to -0.046 SIG
- [def] ucb: 0.6997, -0.035 SIG
- [def] all (ph + contrast + ucb): 0.7342, +0.0001 [-0.0113,+0.0114] n.s.
- [tuned] meta-ph: 0.7345, +0.0004 [-0.0126,+0.0133] n.s.
- [tuned] meta-dbd: 0.7258, -0.0083 n.s.
- [tuned] weight-idf / entropy: 0.7341 / 0.7309, n.s.
- [tuned] weight-contrast: 0.7205, -0.0136 SIG
- [tuned] ucb: 0.7354, +0.0012 [-0.0094,+0.0119] n.s.
- [tuned] combined: 0.7345, identical to [tuned] meta-ph on all headline metrics, so the weighting and UCB add-ons added nothing once PH was on.

**Drift recovery and regret.** Early-post-drift success for [def] meta-ph is 0.730 vs 0.724 for tuned (+0.0066, n.s.). Recovery over the first 300 tasks after drift is 0.721 vs 0.718 (I did not run a paired test on it). [def] meta-ph's regret is 0.1370 vs 0.1360 for tuned (+0.0010, n.s.). Against keyword, [def] meta-ph is +0.0325 SIG on success and +0.057 SIG on early-post. The CI-excluding-0 requirement is not met, because there is no gain over tuned.

**What helped.**
- **[def] meta-ph and [def] all** match hebbian-tuned (CI includes 0, so only "not detectably worse") at 2000 tasks without any hand-tuning. [def] meta-ph is also n.s. vs tuned at 500 (-0.0145) and 6000 (-0.0007), but significantly worse at 1000 (-0.0126). Default eta 0.5 plain loses 0.041, so PH removes that eta sensitivity.
- **[def] all** is n.s. at 500 and 1000 (-0.0097, -0.0091) and 6000 (-0.0013).
- **Default Page-Hinkley is not tuning-free in general.** Temperature 0.05 still matters. Adding temp 0.02 and decay 0.001 on top of default PH made it worse at 2000 (-0.017 SIG).
- **Page-Hinkley is not more robust in the eta x temperature sweep** (held-out, 15 cells, decay .001). Plain ranges 0.677 to 0.739 (mean 0.720). PH ranges 0.538 to 0.735 (mean 0.693). It is worse at the extremes, so the "one setting" claim holds only for the default cell.

**What didn't help.**
- **DBD:** worse than PH everywhere, and significantly worse than tuned at default.
- **Weighting:** no gain when tuned, and losses at defaults. This is expected in this world: all keywords have the same ~10% confound exposure, so per-feature reliability cannot separate confounds. I did not implement per-task, instance-level robust aggregation, which is what would target a confound keyword on a specific task.
- **UCB:** with the base tuned, 0.7354 is within noise. At default settings it adds nothing (0.6997, -0.035).

**Short horizons.** Tuned on 2000 tasks only. Held-out, vs hebbian-tuned:
- **500:** hebbian-tuned 0.6767, below keyword (0.7031, keyword +0.0265 SIG over tuned). No Hebbian variant beats keyword at 500; the best, [tuned] ucb, is 0.6817 (+0.0050, n.s.). So the short-horizon loss is not fixed. eps-greedy is 0.6719.
- **1000:** tuned 0.7179 vs eps-greedy 0.7061 (n.s.) and keyword 0.6982. [tuned] ucb is +0.0037 and [tuned] idf +0.0021, both n.s.
- **6000:** [tuned] meta-ph 0.7764 vs tuned 0.7699, +0.0065 [-0.0041,+0.0171] n.s. eps-greedy is 0.7640. Keyword is 0.7009.

**Other worlds.** I also ran random-structure, no-traps and type-revealed worlds. I only skimmed the no-traps output (keyword success there is about 0.43). That looks like the sim's static keyword map not matching the random structure, so treat keyword numbers in those worlds with suspicion. Hebbian-vs-Hebbian conclusions looked the same; I did not review the random-structure or type-revealed output.

**Recommended default.** Keep the classic rule (all options off) with hebbian-tuned constants: eta 0.05, temperature 0.02, decay 0.001. If you must ship without per-deployment tuning, use `meta: PageHinkley` with the stock config (eta 0.5 ceiling, floor 0.02, meta_decay 0.95, lambda 3, temperature 0.05, decay 0.01). It statistically matches tuned at 2000 and 6000 tasks and fixes the 0.041 loss of default eta, but it is not more robust across the temperature sweep. The tuned PH config (eta 0.5, floor, meta_decay 0.9, decay .001, temp 0.02 or 0.05) also only matches tuned. For short horizons, keyword or eps-greedy is as good or better.
